cases.sentence: Из ___ она узнала о положении Ростовых и о том, как «сын жертвовал собой для матери»; — так говорили в городе.
cases.explain: «городских слухов» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: At the beginning of winter Princess Márya came to Moscow. From reports current in town she learned how the Rostóvs were situated, and how “the son has sacrificed himself for his mother,” as people were saying. “I never expected anything else of him,” said Princess Márya to herself, feeling a joyous sense of her love for him. Remembering her friendly relations with all the Rostóvs which had made her almost a member of the family, she thought it her duty to go to see them. But remembering her relations with Nikoláy in Vorónezh she was shy about doing so. Making a great effort she did however go to call on them a few weeks after her arrival in Moscow.

cases.sentence: Вспоминая свои дружеские и почти ___ ко всему семейству, она считала своею обязанностью ехать к ним.
cases.explain: «родственные отношения» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: At the beginning of winter Princess Márya came to Moscow. From reports current in town she learned how the Rostóvs were situated, and how “the son has sacrificed himself for his mother,” as people were saying. “I never expected anything else of him,” said Princess Márya to herself, feeling a joyous sense of her love for him. Remembering her friendly relations with all the Rostóvs which had made her almost a member of the family, she thought it her duty to go to see them. But remembering her relations with Nikoláy in Vorónezh she was shy about doing so. Making a great effort she did however go to call on them a few weeks after her arrival in Moscow.

cases.sentence: Но, со времени ее посещения, ___ всякий день по нескольку раз заговаривала о ней.
cases.explain: «старая графиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Nikoláy did not reply and tried to avoid speaking of the princess any more. But after her visit the old countess spoke of her several times a day.

cases.sentence: Она очень ___ и всегда тебе нравилась; а теперь вдруг какие-то резоны.
cases.explain: «достойная девушка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Why, you said yourself you don’t want even to see her. She is a very admirable young woman and you always liked her, but now suddenly you have got some notion or other in your head. You hide everything from me.”

cases.sentence: Николай вздыхал, кусая усы, и раскладывал карты, стараясь отвлечь внимание матери на ___.
cases.explain: «другой предмет» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Nikoláy sighed, bit his mustache, and laid out the cards for a patience, trying to divert his mother’s attention to another topic.

cases.sentence: При ___ на лицо Николая, она увидала, что он приехал только для того, чтоб исполнить долг учтивости и решилась твердо держаться в том самом тоне, в котором он обратится к ней.
cases.explain: «первом взгляде» — after the preposition «при», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Her first glance at Nikoláy’s face told her that he had only come to fulfill the demands of politeness, and she firmly resolved to maintain the tone in which he addressed her.

cases.sentence: Они заговорили о здоровье графини, об общих знакомых, о ___ войны и когда прошли те требуемые приличием десять минут, после которых гость может встать, Николай поднялся, прощаясь.
cases.explain: «последних новостях» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: They spoke of the countess’ health, of their mutual friends, of the latest war news, and when the ten minutes required by propriety had elapsed after which a visitor may rise, Nikoláy got up to say goodbye.

cases.sentence: Она сидела так же неподвижно, и на ___ ее выражалось страдание.
cases.explain: «нежном лице» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Nikoláy glanced at her and, wishing to appear not to notice her abstraction, made some remark to Mademoiselle Bourienne and then again looked at the princess. She still sat motionless with a look of suffering on her gentle face. He suddenly felt sorry for her and was vaguely conscious that he might be the cause of the sadness her face expressed. He wished to help her and say something pleasant, but could think of nothing to say.

cases.sentence: — Да, княжна, — сказал наконец Николай, грустно улыбаясь, — недавно кажется, а сколько воды утекло с тех пор, как мы с вами в ___ виделись в Богучарове.
cases.explain: «первый раз» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “Yes, Princess,” said Nikoláy at last with a sad smile, “it doesn’t seem long ago since we first met at Boguchárovo, but how much water has flowed since then! In what distress we all seemed to be then, yet I would give much to bring back that time … but there’s no bringing it back.”

cases.sentence: Княжна пристально глядела ему в глаза своим ___, когда он говорил это.
cases.explain: «лучистым взглядом» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Princess Márya gazed intently into his eyes with her own luminous ones as he said this. She seemed to be trying to fathom the hidden meaning of his words which would explain his feeling for her.

cases.sentence: Она как будто старалась понять тот ___ его слов, который бы объяснил ей его чувство к ней.
cases.explain: «тайный смысл» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Princess Márya gazed intently into his eyes with her own luminous ones as he said this. She seemed to be trying to fathom the hidden meaning of his words which would explain his feeling for her.

cases.sentence: Вот отчего!» говорил ___ в душе княжны Марьи.
cases.explain: «внутренний голос» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “So that’s why! That’s why!” a voice whispered in Princess Márya’s soul. “No, it was not only that gay, kind, and frank look, not only that handsome exterior, that I loved in him. I divined his noble, resolute, self-sacrificing spirit too,” she said to herself. “Yes, he is poor now and I am rich. … Yes, that’s the only reason. … Yes, were it not for that …” And remembering his former tenderness, and looking now at his kind, sorrowful face, she suddenly understood the cause of his coldness.
